title: Paralegal - Real Estate & Projects - Hybrid working
description:
Paralegal - Real Estate & Projects - Hybrid working
Location: Leeds
Salary: Up to £29,000

CRA Consulting are delighted to be working with a well-established, full-service UK law firm with over 150 years' heritage and offices across London, Yorkshire and the Midlands. With approximately 350 employees and a growing international reach, the firm advises a diverse client base including multinational corporations, charities, housing associations, regulators, developers and private individuals.
Due to continued growth, the firm is seeking a Paralegal to join its Real Estate & Projects team in Leeds.

About the Role
This is an exciting opportunity to join a highly regarded and collegiate Real Estate & Projects team. You will support Solicitors and Partners on a wide range of complex property matters, while also building and managing your own caseload.
The role will involve advising and assisting Registered Providers of Social Housing, management companies, landowners, investors, charities and developers on matters including development transactions, stock transfers, inter-group company transfers and ancillary property work.

The Team
The Real Estate team sits at the heart of the firm's practice, with 17 dedicated Partners advising on a broad range of property transactions. The team acts for registered providers of social housing and care homes, private developers on multi-unit schemes, and clients involved in portfolio acquisitions, disposals and open space management.
You will be joining a supportive, open and collaborative department that actively encourages involvement in business development, as well as training and development initiatives.

What You'll Be Doing
- Assisting Solicitors and Fee Earners with the day-to-day management of files.
- Drafting transaction summaries and reports, including Land Agreements, Development Agreements, Transfers and Sectional Agreements.
- Reviewing and reporting on due diligence searches as part of reports on title.
- Producing and inputting reports on title for development site acquisitions.
- Assisting with land transfers, including pre- and post-completion formalities.
- Preparing completion statements, submitting priority searches and liaising directly with clients.
- Undertaking Land Registry applications and dealing with requisitions.
- Drafting ancillary documentation such as Deeds of Covenant, Land Registry certificates and Transfers.
- Meeting departmental targets and adhering to firm procedures and regulatory requirements.

About you:
- Minimum 2:2 Law degree (or equivalent/conversion course).
- 3+ years' experience dealing with the conveyancing process (commercial or residential background considered).
- Strong drafting and legal research skills.
- Excellent organisation and diary management abilities.
- Competent in Microsoft Word, Excel and Outlook.
- Clear and confident communication skills, with the ability to communicate in plain English.
- A methodical approach with strong attention to detail.
- Ability to manage competing priorities and work to tight deadlines.
- Self-motivated, professional and a supportive team player.

Desirable
- Knowledge of a Document Management System (DMS).
- Experience using Partners for Windows (time recording system).

What You'll Get
- The opportunity to join a highly respected and growing Real Estate team.
- Exposure to complex development and social housing transactions.
- Hybrid working with a minimum of 3 office days per week
- A collaborative and supportive working environment.
- Genuine opportunities for professional development and progression.

title: Personal Injury Paralegal
description:
Role: Personal Injury Paralegal
Contract: Remote, permanent, full time
Salary: £30,000 - £35,000
Location: United Kingdom (Remote)

CRA Consulting is currently recruiting for an established and growing Personal Injury team looking to appoint an experienced RTA Fee Earner on a fully remote basis.

This is an excellent opportunity for a confident Personal Injury professional who is comfortable managing their own caseload and wants the flexibility of working remotely while remaining part of a supportive and expanding team.
You will handle a varied caseload of Road Traffic Accident (RTA) claims, covering both pre- and post-litigation matters, including non-portal claims, disputed liability and motorcycle claims.

The successful candidate will have genuine ownership of their files, managing claims from initial instruction through to settlement and, where required, litigation.

The Role

You will manage your own caseload of Fast Track Personal Injury and RTA claims, ensuring matters are progressed efficiently and clients receive a consistently high standard of service.
Your day-to-day responsibilities will include:
- Managing a caseload of pre- and post-litigation RTA claims
- Handling non-portal and Fast Track matters
- Dealing with disputed and denied liability claims
- Managing motorcycle accident claims
- Taking ownership of claims from initial instruction through to settlement
- Assessing liability, quantum and medical evidence
- Reviewing medical reports and assessing compensation
- Preparing schedules of special damages
- Advising clients throughout the claims process
- Negotiating with insurers, third parties and their representatives
- Identifying matters requiring litigation and progressing proceedings accordingly
- Drafting and issuing court proceedings where required
- Completing Directions Questionnaires and complying with court orders and procedural deadlines
- Preparing disclosure and evidential documentation
- Dealing with telephone hearings and other hearings where necessary
- Instructing Counsel, medical experts and other professionals where appropriate
- Conducting relevant legal and case law research
- Maintaining accurate and comprehensive case records
- Working towards internal performance, quality and service standards

About You

We're looking for an experienced RTA / Personal Injury Fee Earner who is confident managing their own caseload and can work effectively with minimal supervision.
Ideally, you will have:
- Experience managing your own RTA caseload
- Experience across both pre- and post-litigation claims
- Experience handling non-portal matters
- Experience dealing with disputed or denied liability
- A good understanding of the Civil Procedure Rules and litigation process
- Strong knowledge of quantum and medical evidence
- Excellent negotiation and client management skills
- Strong written and verbal communication skills
- Excellent organisation and time management
- The ability to manage a busy caseload and competing deadlines
- Strong attention to detail and file management
- Experience using case management systems and Microsoft Office
- The ability to work independently within a fully remote environment
- A practical and solutions-focused approach

A Solicitor or CILEX practitioner with relevant practising rights would be advantageous, although experienced Fee Earners without these qualifications will also be considered.

What's on Offer?
- Fully remote working
- An established and growing Personal Injury team
- A varied RTA and Fast Track caseload
- The opportunity to manage your own caseload
- Supportive and collaborative colleagues
- Ongoing training and professional development
- Genuine autonomy and flexibility
- Long-term career development within Personal Injury

Interested?

If you're an experienced RTA Fee Earner or Fast Track Fee Earner looking for a fully remote opportunity, we'd be keen to hear from you.
For further information or a confidential discussion about the role, please contact Oliver Birch at CRA Consulting.

title: Claims Handler
description:
Claims Handler

Leeds Hybrid Working (4 Days Office / 1 Day Home)

Build your claims career with a highly respected and award-winning UK claims team

Claims is about more than resolving losses. It's about delivering exceptional service, building trusted relationships and supporting customers when they need it most.

We're looking for a Claims Handler to join a Prompt Resolution Team in Leeds. Whether you already have property claims experience or are looking to broaden your insurance career, this is an opportunity to join a supportive team that develops future claims specialists, senior handlers and leaders.

Many experienced claims professionals have started their careers within this team, making it an excellent entry point into the wider claims function.

Why this role is different:

This isn't a call centre environment.

You'll manage your own portfolio of claims, take ownership of decisions and build relationships with brokers, customers and third parties.

You'll gain exposure to a wide variety of claims, with a particular focus on property claims, whilst also developing experience across liability and injury matters. This breadth of exposure gives you genuine opportunities to shape your future career within claims.

You'll be joining a team recognised for:
- Exceptional customer service
- Fast and responsive claims handling
- Strong broker relationships
- Technical expertise
- High-quality claims performance

What you'll be doing:

You'll manage a varied caseload of claims from first notification through to resolution, taking ownership of customer outcomes and delivering excellent service throughout.

Key responsibilities include:
- Managing low-value property damage claims
- Handling Employers' Liability and Public Liability claims
- Reviewing claims information and policy coverage
- Liaising with customers, brokers, loss adjusters and third parties
- Making proactive outbound calls to progress claims efficiently
- Prioritising and managing your own workload
- Delivering excellent customer and broker service
- Working to agreed service standards and response times
- Building strong relationships across the business and wider claims network

You'll handle a broad range of property claims including:
- Escape of water
- Storm damage
- Fire damage
- Theft
- Accidental damage
- Property and equipment losses
- Domestic and commercial property matters

What we're looking for:

We're particularly interested in speaking with individuals who have experience handling:

Property Claims
- Household claims
- Personal lines property claims
- Domestic property claims
- Commercial property claims
- First-party property claims

About the organisation

We're proud of our people-first culture and reputation for delivering outstanding claims service.

If you're looking for a role where you'll be trusted, developed and given genuine opportunities to progress your career, we'd love to hear from you.

We celebrate the value of a diverse workforce that brings experience and expertise from a wide variety of backgrounds and life circumstances. Whatever your background, if you feel you meet the requirements of this role, we want to hear from you.

We are an equal opportunity employer and value diversity. We do not discriminate on the basis of race, religion, colour, national origin, sex, gender, gender expression, sexual orientation, age, marital status, veteran status or disability status.

All such information from any source is to be regarded as strictly confidential Information relating to patients, carers, colleagues, other healthcare workers or the business of the practice may only be divulged to authorised persons in accordance with the practice policies and procedures relating to confidentiality and the protection of personal and sensitive data. Health & Safety : The post-holder will assist in promoting and maintaining their own and others health, safety and security as defined in the practice Health & Safety Policy, to include: Using personal security systems within the workplace according to practice guidelines Identifying the risks involved in work activities and undertaking such activities in a way that manages those risks Making effective use of training to update knowledge and skills Using appropriate infection control procedures, maintaining work areas in a tidy and safe way and free from hazards Reporting potential risks identified. Equality and Diversity : The post-holder will support the equality, diversity and rights of patients, carers and colleagues, to include: Acting in a way that recognizes the importance of peoples rights, interpreting them in a way that is consistent with practice procedures and policies, and current legislation Respecting the privacy, dignity, needs and beliefs of patients, carers and colleagues Behaving in a manner which is welcoming to and of the individual, is non-judgmental and respects their circumstances, feelings priorities and rights. Personal/Professional Development : The post-holder will participate in any training programme implemented by the practice as part of this employment, such training to include: Participation in an annual individual performance review, including taking responsibility for maintaining a record of own personal and/or professional development Taking responsibility for own development, learning and performance and demonstrating skills and activities to others who are undertaking similar work. Quality : The post-holder will strive to maintain quality within the practice, and will: Alert other team members to issues of quality and risk Assess own performance and take accountability for own actions, either directly or under supervision Contribute to the effectiveness of the team by reflecting on own and team activities and making suggestions on ways to improve and enhance the teams performance Work effectively with individuals in other agencies to meet patients needs Effectively manage own time, workload and resources. Communication : The post-holder should recognize the importance of effective communication within the team and will strive to: Communicate effectively with other team members Communicate effectively with patients and carers Recognize peoples needs for alternative methods of communication and respond accordingly. Contribution to the Implementation of Services : The post-holder will: Apply practice policies, standards and guidance Discuss with other members of the team how the policies, standards and guidelines will affect own work Participate in audit where appropriate. Important note: This Job description reflects the duties we currently anticipate the post holder undertaking. However, the duties required of the post holder could change over time. You will be expected to undertake tasks/duties required to maintain the efficient running of the Practice, which may not be detailed on this Job description, but which are commensurate with your grade and within your capabilities. Any permanent changes to this Job description will be made following consultation with the post holder.

title: Administrative Assistant
description: An exciting opportunity has arisen for an Administrative Assistant to join the existing Quality Team within Specialty and Integrated Medicine (SIM) Clinical Service Unit. We are small, experienced team who are motivated to work with our clinical teams to ensure we provide the best possible care to our patients. We are seeking an enthusiastic and motivated individual with excellent attention to detail to join our team. The candidate will be responsible for providing administrative support to the Lead Nurses for Clinical Quality and Education and the Quality Manager. Responsibilities will include organisation of complex meetings, preparation of agendas, data sets and Powerpoint slides, and taking high quality, accurate minutes. The post holder will also be responsible for co-ordinating the CSUs complaints, liaising with nursing, medical and management teams to ensure timely responses and feeding back at the weekly complaints huddle. Applicants should have a broad range of administration skills, particularly the ability to take high quality, detailed minutes at speed, with excellent attention to detail. It is essential that the person is able to work under pressure, within a team and autonomously, and prioritise their work load accordingly with excellent organisational skills. The role requires extensive use of Microsoft Office applications such as Excel, Word and PowerPoint. Are you passionate about making a difference? Are you looking for an opportunity to support our clinical teams in delivering excellent quality care? Do you have excellent administrative and organisational skills? If the answer is yes, we would love to hear from you. For questions about this job, contact: Name. Emma Tunnacliffe Position Quality Manager Email emma.tunnacliffe@nhs.net Phone number 07899 021837 or 0113 20 64654 Shortlisting Date: 16/10/2026 Interview Date: 27/10/2026 & 28/10/2026 Why you should join our Team Specialty & Integrated Medicine (SIM) Clinical Service Unit (CSU) Specialty & Integrated Medicine (SIM) is home to a variety of services at the Trust. There are wards covering the following specialties: General Medicine, Older People’s Medicine, Infectious Diseases/Travel Medicine, Diabetes and Endocrinology. We also have outpatient facilities for Diabetes, Endocrinology, Intravenous Antibiotics (OPAT), HIV and Sexual Health. SIM CSU Quality Team The team comprises of two Lead Nurses for Clinical Quality and Education, one Quality Manager and this post, Quality Governance and Complaints Co-ordinator. We are a small, friendly team who work closely together and share a passion for working with the wider SIM CSU teams to ensure our patients receive the best possible care. The role of the Administrative Assistant is to provide a comprehensive administrative support to the Quality Team and wider team in SIM CSU (where it is Quality Governance related). This includes (but is not limited to): Co-ordinating multiple meetings per month by booking meeting rooms, preparing and circulating agendas, preparing slides or other documents. Attending the meetings and producing high quality minutes in a timely manner. Collating and co-ordinating the CSU’s complaint responses and ensuring deadlines are met, liaising with the clinical teams to achieve this. Uploading action logs from complaints to Datix. Tracking patient safety reviews and investigations and uploading action logs to Datix. Providing administrative support to the Quality Manager and Lead Nurses for Clinical Quality in the oversight of the Quality Governance portfolio including: Complaints and PALS Incidents Duty of Candour Clinical guidelines/NICE guidance Friends and Family Test Audit Mortality and morbidity reviews Assist and support the wider SIM CSU teams with Quality Governance related queries. Our Trust values The Leeds Way is working together to support each other and deliver the best possible care to patients. We are…. Responsible Open and Honest One Team Kind Our Trust priorities Our purpose: Excellent, safe and sustainable care for every patient every time Our priorities: People Improvement and Innovation Partnerships Outcomes To comply with UK Government regulations on Skilled Worker sponsorship, Leeds Teaching Hospital NHS Trust is unable to provide sponsorship to applicants who do not meet the eligibility criteria or the salary threshold concessions set out under the Skilled Worker visa route. Please take this into consideration before submitting your application. Full guidance on these concessions, including details of who may qualify, can be found here. We reserve the right to close this advert early if we receive a high number of suitable applications.

title: Receptionist
description: The post-holder will be working with the rest of the team at Beechwood Medical Centre. You will mainly be working on the reception desk dealing with patients face to face. The role is an afternoon and morning role and you will work alongside another team member who will be working on the reception desk with you. The hours are quite specific in order to cover the site for all of the hours we are open. If you have worked in general practice or primary care before that would be useful but it is not essential all of the training will be given. The following are the core responsibilities of the receptionist. There may be, on occasion, a requirement to carry out other tasks; this will depend on factors such as workload and staffing levels as directed by the Practice Operations Manager: a. Carry out administrative duties associated with working in a busy General Practice. b. Deal with all patients and visitors to the practice in a face to face environment. c. Book, change and cancel appointments for patients in line with current arrangements. d. Deal with things, like prescription requests, patient registrations, patient signposting and carrying out duties as requested by the Practice Operations Manager, Business Manager or Partners e. To work with other team members and support the practice operationally. This may included things like ordering, room allocations, photocopying, post management and other general reception duties. The hours for this role are very specific in order to cover the surgery for the hours we are open: Monday - 8.00am - 12.45pm Tuesday - 8.00am - 2.15pm (with a 15 minute tea break) Wednesday - 12.30pm - 6.30pm Thursday - 1.15pm - 6.30pm Friday - 1.45pm - 6.30pm Total weekly hours - 27.0 You MUST be able to work these hours, although we will have a small degree of flexability. The post-holder will be working with the rest of the team at Beechwood Medical Centre. You will be working on the reception in a face to face environment . The hours are quite specific in order to cover the site for all of the hours we are open. If you have worked in general practice or primary care before that would be useful but it is not essential all of the training will be given.

title: Medical Administrator
description: Previous applicants need not apply. Oakwood Lane Medical Practice is delighted to offer an opportunity for a dedicated Medical Administrator to join our friendly, forward thinking team. We care for a diverse population of over 14,000 patients and pride ourselves on delivering high quality, patient centred healthcare. We are looking for an enthusiastic, organised and proactive administrator who is passionate about supporting excellent patient care. You will play a key role in ensuring patients receive the right care at the right time, contributing to the smooth and efficient running of the practice. Join us and become part of a supportive, inclusive and dynamic team committed to delivering outstanding healthcare. Part-t ime role 24-28 hours per week. Must be able to work a Thursday. Document and Record Management Process, scan and code incoming clinical correspondence. Assign documents to the correct clinician or administrative team promptly and accurately. Identify and escalate urgent or clinically significant information. Liaise with clinicians to clarify documentation queries and ensure appropriate action. Maintain accurate patient records using workflow systems. Process incoming and outgoing patient records. Referral Administration Complete and submit patient referrals to specialists and external providers, ensuring all documentation is accurate and complete. Take ownership of referrals from initiation to completion, including monitoring rejections and responses. Provide clear information to patients regarding referral pathways and progress. Ensure all referral communications are documented and filed appropriately. Insurance and Third Party Requests Manage insurance forms, medical reports and third party documentation with accuracy and compliance. Support patients and staff with queries relating to access to medical records and permissions. General Administrative Support Provide flexible administrative cover across departments as required. Support statutory and contractual practice obligations. Assist with ad-hoc administrative tasks to ensure smooth day to day operations. Work collaboratively with colleagues and contribute to continuous improvement initiatives. Process, scan and code incoming clinical correspondence including hospital letters, discharge summaries, ambulance notifications and out of hours reports. Review correspondence and ensure documents are attached to the correct patient record. Code or free text clinical information on to the patient record. Assign documents to the appropriate clinician or administrative team promptly and accurately. Identify urgent, abnormal or clinically significant information and escalate in accordance with practice procedures. Liaise with clinical staff to clarify documentation queries and ensure appropriate actions are completed. Maintain accurate patient records using practice workflow and clinical systems. Process incoming and outgoing patient records in accordance with NHS and practice procedures, ensuring records are transferred, received and managed accurately and securely. Monitor workflow queues to ensure correspondence is processed within agreed timescales. Deal with queries relating to correspondence management and document processing. Complete and submit referrals to secondary care, community services and external providers, ensuring all supporting documentation is accurate and complete. Take ownership of referrals from initiation through to completion. Monitor referral progress, including rejected referrals, requests for further information and provider responses. Liaise with clinicians to obtain information required to support referrals. Provide patients with information regarding referral pathways, appointments and progress where appropriate. Ensure all referral activity, communications and outcomes are accurately documented and filed within the patient record. Support the practice in achieving referral processing targets and standards. Manage insurance reports, medical reports and third-party documentation requests in accordance with practice procedures and relevant legislation. Ensure documentation is completed accurately and within agreed timescales. Support patients and staff with queries relating to access to medical records, consent and permissions. Maintain accurate records of requests, actions and outcomes. Escalate complex or sensitive requests to the appropriate manager or clinician. Statutory and Contractual Support Support the management of requests for information, reports and returns relating to the practice's statutory and contractual obligations. Assist with administrative processes required to support regulatory, contractual and operational requirements. Undertake any other reasonable duties requested by the management team in support of the practice's business operations.
